proof.text: The normalized etale comparison is supplied directly by [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. Apply its clauses (1)--(3) to $e=u$ and to the base-changed map $e=v$: clause (1) identifies $\rho_{e,K}\theta_{e,K}$ with the tensor unit constraint, clause (2) gives identity, composition and Cartesian base-change normalization, and clause (3) gives the corresponding dualizing comparison $E_{e,h}$ and its unit normalization. The maps $a_X$ and $a_Z$ are smooth by [sk-lem-regular-smooth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], the base change $v$ is etale, and by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] smoothness is preserved under base change and composition, with the relative-dimension data preserved; hence the induced structure maps $a_U=a_X\circ u$ and $a_V=a_Z\circ v$ are smooth. The d=0 chart clause of [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization] says that the standard section and rank-zero bundle comparisons are identities (P_0=id), so the normalized diagonal orientation for a relative-dimension-zero etale map is exactly $\eta_e$, the unit orientation. That clause is stated on affine charts $U'\subseteq e^{-1}V'$, $V'$ affine, where $e|_{U'}:U'\to V'=\mathbf A^0_{V'}$ is itself the etale coordinate morphism, and it commutes with open restriction; $\eta_e$ restricts to $\eta_{e|_{U'}}$ by clause (2) of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. Both maps $\omega_e\to\Lambda_U$ are maps between objects isomorphic (via $\eta_e$) to the degree-zero sheaf $\Lambda_U$, so they are maps of sheaves and agree globally because they agree on an open cover. The relative-dimension-zero etale hypotheses are those of [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus the $Ru^!\cong Lu^*$ and $Rv^!\cong Lv^*$ in the statement are the specified normalized comparisons, and their smooth orientations are the unit orientations; no independently chosen adjunction comparison is introduced. Hypotheses of [pur9-rg-def-phi] for $i_U$: let $z'\in V$, with images $z=v(z')\in Z$ and $x=i(z)\in X$. On affine charts $u$ and $v$ are given by etale ring maps [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{U,i_U(z')}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z'}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}$; with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ from [sk-lem-regular-smooth] this is the dimension equality of [def-pur-regular-immersion] for $i_U$. Since $V=Z\times_XU$, $\mathcal O_{V,z'}=\mathcal O_{U,i_U(z')}/I_x\mathcal O_{U,i_U(z')}$, so the ideal of $i_U$ at $z'$ is generated by the images of generators $f_1,\dots,f_c$ of $I_x$ forming an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-regular sequence [def-pur-regular-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The local map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{U,i_U(z')}$ is flat [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism]; tensoring the injective multiplications by $f_j$ on $\mathcal O_{X,x}/(f_1,\dots,f_{j-1})$ with it keeps them injective, and the final quotient $\mathcal O_{V,z'}$ is a nonzero local ring, so the images form an $\mathcal O_{U,i_U(z')}$-regular sequence of length $c$ (the empty sequence when $c=0$). Finally $a_V$ is smooth, hence affine-locally given by smooth $k$-algebras [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], which are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] with regular local rings [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]; so $V$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. $U$ and $V$ are separated of finite type over $k$ ($V$ being closed in $U$). Thus $\Phi_{i_U}$ is defined.

Write $c_{g,f,L}:R(gf)^!L\to Rf^!Rg^!L$ for the specified comparison of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]. Its invertibility and associative/unital composition law are part of the exceptional composition clause of [sk-thm-sf-compatibility]. Apply the comparison to $(i_U,u)$ and $(i,v)$. The fibre-product identity $u\circ i_U=i\circ v$ identifies the middle terms literally. By clause (2) of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], the normalized $\rho$-comparisons preserve this composition and the identity maps. Therefore the inverse of $c_{u,i_U}$, followed by $c_{i,v}$ and the normalized identifications $Ru^!\cong Lu^*$ and $Rv^!\cong Lv^*$, is exactly the displayed five-arrow pasting $B_{u,i}$, and every arrow is an isomorphism.

The two orientation factors in [pur9-rg-def-phi] are the specified diagonal orientations of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. The d=0 chart clause of [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization] identifies the rank-zero diagonal orientation with the unit orientation $\eta_e$. At the coefficient unit, the defining transpose in [def-pur-co-smoothness](2) reduces to the unit constraint: the proper projection with unit coefficient is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and the open tensor comparison in [def-exchange-projection] is the unitor. Hence $\theta_{f,\Lambda}$ is the unit constraint, with the same canonical reassociation used in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Apply [thm-pur-composition-coherence] to the actual smooth factorizations $a_U=a_X\circ u$ and $a_V=a_Z\circ v$. Since $u$ and $v$ are etale of relative dimension zero, clause (3) of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] identifies the resulting $E_{e,h}$ and $\sigma_{e,h}$ with these unit-normalized pullbacks. Thus the pulled-back diagonal orientation factors are exactly the orientation factors for $a_U$ and $a_V$, with no Cartesian square asserted where none exists.

For $L=\Lambda(c)[2c]$ and for each component dimension, the co-projection isomorphisms are those of [lem-pur-coprojection]. The twist sheaf is locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], and its pullback and tensor reassociation are fixed by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The general compatibility lemma [lem-pur-etale-coprojection-rho-compatibility] applies to the square $(i_U,u,v,i)$ and says precisely that these co-projection maps commute with the normalized $\rho$-comparisons and the exceptional composition pasting defining $B_{u,i}$. Its hypotheses are met by the etale normalization clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. The projection transformation used in the co-projection definition is the specified one from [def-exchange-projection], so this is compatibility of the chosen maps rather than an arbitrary isomorphism.

Expand the composite defining $\Phi_i$ in [pur9-rg-def-phi]. Its factors are the inverse orientation for $a_Z$, the exceptional composition comparison for $a_Z=a_X\circ i$, the inverse orientation for $a_X$, and the twist/co-projection comparisons. For $a_X\circ u\circ i_U=a_X\circ i\circ v$, clause (2) of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] and the associative composition law in [sk-thm-sf-compatibility] identify the two pastings of the exceptional comparisons. Step 3 identifies the pulled-back orientation factors, and Step 4 (via [lem-pur-etale-coprojection-rho-compatibility]) identifies each pulled-back co-projection with the co-projection after base change. Pasting these equalities in the order of the defining composite gives $B_{u,i}\circ\Phi_{i_U}=Lv^*\Phi_i$. The argument is componentwise: [sk-lem-regular-smooth] supplies the smooth structure maps, while [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] supplies etale base-change stability and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] supplies smoothness under base change/composition and the dimension relation, while [pur9-rg-def-phi] assembles the componentwise maps over the disjoint union. The same calculation covers varying component dimensions and makes no Kummer or fundamental-class identification.

title: Étale locality of the exceptional orientation
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient datum $k,\ell,E,n,\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $c\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with $X$ smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $Z$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Use the specified diagonal smooth orientations $\Pi_{a_X}$ and $\Pi_{a_Z}$ of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], and let $\Phi_i:\Lambda_Z\to Ri^!(\Lambda_X(c)[2c])$ be the composite of [pur9-rg-def-phi], with the adjunction-preserving exceptional composition comparison of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]. Let $u:U\to X$ be an etale morphism with $U$ separated and finite type over $k$, and put $V=Z\times_XU$, with maps $v:V\to Z$ and $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $v$ is etale, and by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] the structure maps $a_U=a_X\circ u$ and $a_V=a_Z\circ v$ are smooth with the inherited relative dimensions. The pair $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$ again satisfies the hypotheses above (a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $c$ [def-pur-regular-immersion], $U$ smooth over $k$, $V$ regular), so $\Phi_{i_U}$ is defined by [pur9-rg-def-phi].

The canonical identifications $Ru^!\cong Lu^*$ and $Rv^!\cong Lv^*$ on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] identify their relative-dimension-zero smooth orientations with the unit orientations. The resulting comparison
$$B_{u,i}:Ri_U^!Lu^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_U^!Ru^!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(ui_U)^!=R(iv)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv^!Ri^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Lv^*Ri^!$$
is compatible with the co-projection maps for Tate shifts [lem-pur-coprojection] and satisfies
$$B_{u,i}\circ\Phi_{i_U}=Lv^*\Phi_i,$$
using $Lv^*\Lambda_Z=\Lambda_V$ and $Lu^*\Lambda_X(c)=\Lambda_U(c)$. The same assertion applies componentwise when the smooth dimensions vary. This is an assertion about the specified orientation composite, without identifying it with any Kummer or fundamental class.
